<execute-bead>
  <instructions>
You are executing one bead in an isolated DDx execution worktree. The bead's <description> and <acceptance> are the contract: every AC must be provably satisfied by a specific code, test, or file after your commit.

## Step 0: size check

Too big if any holds:

- More than ~6 ACs spanning unrelated subsystems.
- AC mixes design, implementation, integration tests, and docs.
- Description names multiple feature-sized pieces.
- More than ~500 lines across ~5+ files in unrelated packages.
- If the bead description exceeds 8000 bytes, use a split-first pass.
- Auto-decomposition is capped at depth 2: root beads may split once, children once more; reject third-level splits with an explanation.

If too big, decompose:

1. `ddx bead create` for each child (copy parent's labels and spec-id).
2. `ddx bead dep add <child-id> <parent-id>` to record edges.
3. `ddx bead update <parent-id> --notes 'decomposed into <child-ids>'`.
4. Write `no_changes_rationale.txt` under the bead metadata `bundle` path with child IDs, then stop.

Decomposition alone is success. Do not mix it with implementation.

## How to work

- Read first. If the bead names files, specs, or prior beads, read them before editing — do not guess.
- Cross-reference each AC to concrete evidence (test, file, function) before committing. If you cannot point at it, it is not done.
- Run the project's test and lint commands before committing. **Do not commit red code** — fix failures first.
- Run git/index mutations sequentially; do not use parallel tool calls for `git add`, `git commit`, or other staging/commit commands.
- Stage with `git add <specific-paths>`; never `git add -A` (the worktree may have unrelated WIP).
- If `lefthook run pre-commit` depends on staged files, rerun it after staging the exact commit set. A `no-staged-files` run is not acceptance evidence.
- Commit exactly once when green; conventional-commit subject ending with `[<bead-id>]`. Stop after the commit.
- Do not modify files outside the bead's scope.
- Current-bead lifecycle is orchestrator-owned. Do not run `ddx bead update <bead-id> --claim`, `ddx bead update <bead-id> --status <status>`, `ddx bead update <bead-id> --unclaim`, or `ddx bead close <bead-id>`. Step 0 still allows `ddx bead create`, `ddx bead dep add`, and `ddx bead update <parent-id> --notes 'decomposed into <child-ids>'`.
- If you cannot finish, write `no_changes_rationale.txt` under the bead metadata `bundle` path before exiting. No commit or rationale ⇒ DDx records `no_evidence_produced`.

## no_changes contract

The `no_changes_rationale.txt` file under the bead metadata `bundle` path must contain one of:

- `verification_command: <cmd>` — repo cwd; exit 0 closes, nonzero rejects.
- `status: open` + `reason: <retryable>` — open, smart retry.
- `status: proposed` + `reason: <operator needed>` — operator lane.
- `status: blocked` + `reason: <external blocker>` — blocked lane.

No pseudo-statuses. Bare rationales and `status: needs_investigation` are rejected.

For orchestrator decomposition, add `orchestrator_action: decompose` alongside `status: open`.

## Reports

Reports go under the bead metadata `bundle` path in `.ddx/executions/`. **Never write reports to `/tmp` or outside the repo**. Use a named in-repo path when given; otherwise write `<short-name>.md` there. Commit it with the code.

## Mode and overrides

DDX_MODE=bead_execution: edit code/docs for bead AC. Only broad queue-steward default is overridden; tracker, merge-policy, verification, safety stay active. Bead description/AC override CLAUDE.md, AGENTS.md, and defaults.

## Review gate

- The review is a gate, not an escape hatch — meet every AC in this pass.
- Address every BLOCKING `<review-findings>` item; do not declare `no_changes` with blocking findings open.

## Constraints

- Work only inside this execution worktree.
- Keep `.ddx/executions/` intact — DDx uses it as execution evidence.
- **Never run `ddx init`** — the workspace is initialized.
- Do not modify files outside the bead's named scope.
- Do not rewrite CLAUDE.md, AGENTS.md, or other instruction files unless the bead asks.

## When the work is done

After the commit succeeds and every AC is verified, stop. Return control to the orchestrator.
  </instructions>
  <bead id="fizeau-50b6f055">
    <title>harnesses: kill the spawned process group on every exit path (not just ctx-cancel) — gemini/claude/codex subprocesses orphan and leak</title>
    <description>
PROBLEM
Running `fiz --provider local` (and long bench sessions) leaks orphaned harness subprocesses. Observed 2026-05-27 on the dev host: 366 leaked `gemini` node processes, ~14 GB RSS, accumulated over 15+ hours, all reparented to PID 1 (parents long dead). The same shape applies to any harness whose CLI spawns its own children: on a NORMAL (successful) run the spawned process group is never signaled, so any grandchild the harness CLI itself forked survives fizeau's exit and orphans.

ROOT CAUSE (file:line)
- Every harness runner creates a fresh process group via setProcessGroupAttr (Setpgid=true) in internal/harnesses/{harness}/runner_unix.go and ships a killProcessGroup helper that signals the negative pgid.
- internal/harnesses/gemini/runner.go:274-282 — the cleanup goroutine calls killProcessGroup(cmd) ONLY on `<-ctx.Done()`. On normal completion the `<-stdoutReady` branch wins and the goroutine returns without killing the group. cmd.Wait() (runner.go:286) reaps only the direct child; any process the gemini CLI itself spawned (the gemini main -> gemini worker pairs seen in `ps`) stays in the group, un-signaled, and orphans to PID 1.
- killProcessGroup (internal/harnesses/{harness}/runner_unix.go) sends a single SIGTERM with no SIGKILL escalation, so even on cancel/timeout a child that ignores SIGTERM survives.
- A stale-harness reaper exists (service_stale_harness_reaper.go + service_stale_harness_reaper_unix.go terminateOwnedProcessGroup, SIGTERM->SIGKILL) but NOTHING in the runners registers a harness-sessions/*.json record at cmd.Start(), so the reaper has no PIDs/PGIDs to act on and is effectively a no-op for these leaks.
- Audit the sibling runners for the same conditional-cleanup shape: internal/harnesses/claude/runner.go:263 & :426, internal/harnesses/codex/runner.go:233, internal/harnesses/pi/runner.go:207, internal/harnesses/opencode/runner.go:204 (spawn via internal/harnesses/exec.go:18 HarnessCommand).

PROPOSED FIX
1. Kill the process group on EVERY exit path of every harness runner (success, error, timeout, cancel) — not only on ctx cancellation. e.g. ensure the cleanup goroutine always calls killProcessGroup before the runner returns, or `defer killProcessGroup(cmd)` immediately after a successful Start.
2. Escalate killProcessGroup to SIGTERM -> bounded grace -> SIGKILL (mirror terminateOwnedProcessGroup in service_stale_harness_reaper_unix.go) so stubborn grandchildren cannot survive.
3. Backstop: either register a (pid,pgid) session record at cmd.Start() that the stale-harness reaper consumes, or remove the dead reaper infra and document why. Wire one path so the reaper is not silently inert.

NON-SCOPE
- Harness output parsing/streaming behavior is unchanged.
- Windows process-group semantics (only *_unix.go is covered) — out of scope; note if it matters.
- The claude-tui PTY-pool orphan reaper (fizeau-a14eba0c) is a distinct mechanism; cross-ref only.

CROSS-REF: fizeau-a14eba0c (claude-tui PTY orphan reaper).
    </description>
    <acceptance>
1. After a NORMAL (successful) harness run, no subprocess spawned by that run survives the runner's return: a test spawns a fake provider binary that forks a long-lived grandchild, runs it through the runner to a "success" outcome, and asserts the grandchild process is gone (not reparented to PID 1) once the runner returns. Lives in internal/harnesses (gemini runner at minimum).
2. The process-group kill fires on ALL outcomes — success, error, timeout, and cancel — verified by a table test over those outcomes (the gemini runner.go:274-282 conditional-cleanup gap is closed, and sibling runners are audited/fixed for the same shape).
3. killProcessGroup escalates SIGTERM -> bounded grace -> SIGKILL, verified by a test using a child that ignores SIGTERM.
4. Backstop wired: either harness runners register a (pid,pgid) session record consumed by the stale-harness reaper (with a test proving a leaked group is reaped), OR the unused reaper infra is removed. Not left silently inert.
5. go test ./... green; lint passes.
    </acceptance>

data.output:
Implemented the runner-side leak fix in `internal/harnesses/{gemini,claude,codex,pi,opencode}`:

- Each Unix `killProcessGroup` now escalates `SIGTERM -> 100ms grace -> SIGKILL`.
- Each runner now cleans up on every exit path, not just cancellation.
- The stale-harness reaper path was removed from `service.go` and the dead reaper files were deleted.
- Added a regression test in [internal/harnesses/gemini/runner_unix_test.go](/Users/erik/Projects/.ddx-exec-wt/.execute-bead-clone-fizeau-50b6f055-20260527T083726-8e573fa3/internal/harnesses/gemini/runner_unix_test.go) that exercises success, error, timeout, and cancel with a detached grandchild that ignores `SIGTERM`.

Verification:
- `go test ./internal/harnesses/gemini ./internal/harnesses/codex ./internal/harnesses/pi ./internal/harnesses/opencode ./internal/harnesses/claude` passes.
- `go test ./...` is still red in `internal/harnesses/capability_matrix_test.go` on pre-existing docs/matrix expectations unrelated to this bead.

Because of that blocker, I wrote the execution note at [`.ddx/executions/20260527T083726-8e573fa3/no_changes_rationale.txt`](/Users/erik/Projects/.ddx-exec-wt/.execute-bead-clone-fizeau-50b6f055-20260527T083726-8e573fa3/.ddx/executions/20260527T083726-8e573fa3/no_changes_rationale.txt). No commit was made.
